credentials.description: OAuth token from your Yango Delivery account (Integration tab, Get token); changing the account password invalidates it

parameters.name: claim_id
parameters.description: Claim ID received at the claim creation stage Passed as a query parameter.

example_prompt: Find out whether cancelling a Yango Delivery claim is still free, paid or no longer possible.
gotchas: Authenticate with 'Authorization: Bearer <OAuth token>'. The token comes from your Yango Delivery account (log in with the credentials your Yango Delivery manager gives you, Integration tab, Get token). It remains valid indefinitely, but changing the account password invalidates it; an invalid token answers 401 unauthorized.
cancel_state is free, paid or unavailable. Pass free or paid unchanged to cancel_delivery_claim. The reference doesn't describe unavailable: don't call cancel_delivery_claim with it.

Free cancellation lasts until the courier arrives at the pickup point (all pages agree). The paid window is contradictory: the getting-started page and the FAQ make cancellation paid once the courier has arrived but hasn't picked up the items, while the cancel reference says paid cancellation is available before the courier starts moving to the pickup point. Rely on cancel_state from get_cancellation_terms, never on the status alone.
After the courier has picked up the items, only the support service can cancel the order.
Accept-Language is a required header on this endpoint (e.g. en); this example sends en.

Errors return { code, message }: branch on code. Documented on this endpoint: 400 bad_request; 404 not_found. The error guide adds 401 unauthorized (invalid token) and 500 (try again or change the request).
open_questions: No test environment is documented: the API reference gives only the service URL b2b.delivery.yango.tech, and confirming a claim starts a real courier search. Ask your Yango Delivery manager for a test account.
